name: CorelDRAW
subcategory: vector graphics and print production suite
tagline: Professional vector illustration, layout and print production suite for Windows and macOS.

pricing.basis: subscription, also sold as a perpetual license
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely one-shot a vector editor: rectangles, beziers, boolean ops, SVG export. What you cannot one-shot is thirty-plus years of bezier editing ergonomics, CMYK and spot color handling, Pantone libraries, PDF/X and PostScript output that a commercial printer will actually accept, font handling across thousands of typefaces, and CDR file compatibility with whoever sends you files. CorelDRAW's buyers are mostly sign shops, print shops, apparel and engraving businesses whose entire workflow and file archive live in it. An agent-built editor will feel fine for ten minutes and then you will hit node snapping, color profiles, or a 400-object layout and stop. Also worth saying out loud: Inkscape is free and already much further along than anything you will build this weekend.
coreLoopDIY: A browser-based SVG editor where you draw shapes and bezier paths, edit nodes, apply fills and strokes, arrange layers, and export clean SVG or PNG.
whatYouLose: CMYK, spot color, Pantone libraries and ICC color management, so nothing you make is print-ready
PDF/X, EPS and PostScript output that commercial printers accept without argument
CDR and AI file import, which is how files actually arrive from clients and vendors
Decades of node editing, snapping, alignment and typography ergonomics that make large layouts bearable
The rest of the suite: photo editing, font management, tracing, multi-page layout, and the plugin ecosystem
moatNotes: The real lock-in is the print pipeline and the archive of CDR files sitting on a sign shop's server.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the output has to come out of a physical machine: a wide-format printer, a vinyl cutter, a laser engraver, a screen press. That means color accuracy, correct separations, correct file formats, and a toolchain the operator already knows cold. A personal vector editor can make a nice logo. It cannot make a file a print vendor will run without a phone call. And for the people who just want to draw vectors for the web, the honest answer is not to build anything at all, it is to open Inkscape or Figma.
notes: A weekend SVG editor is a fun project and a bad CorelDRAW. The moat is the print production pipeline: CMYK, spot colors, PDF/X, and a generation of shop operators with muscle memory and a folder of CDR files.
prompt:
Build a local, browser-based vector drawing app called "Vectorish". Static site, no backend, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- TypeScript, Vite, no UI framework beyond plain DOM and a small state store you write yourself.
- Render the artwork as live SVG in the DOM. Do not use canvas. The SVG document IS the model.
- Zustand-free: one module with a document object, an undo stack of immutable snapshots, and subscriber callbacks.
- Tailwind for the chrome only. No component library.

In scope:
- Tools: select, rectangle, ellipse, line, pen (click for corner nodes, drag for smooth bezier handles), text.
- Direct node editing: click a path with the node tool, drag anchors and handles, add or delete a node, toggle corner vs smooth.
- Transform: move, scale with corner handles, rotate, with Shift to constrain and Alt to duplicate.
- Fill and stroke panel: solid RGB fill, stroke color, stroke width, dash array, opacity. Linear gradients if time allows.
- Boolean ops on two selected closed paths: union, subtract, intersect. Use the paper.js library for the geometry, do not hand-roll it.
- Layers panel: reorder, rename, hide, lock.
- Snapping: to a configurable grid and to other objects' edges and centers, with visible guide lines.
- Zoom and pan: scroll to pan, Ctrl+scroll to zoom, key to fit artwork.
- Undo/redo with Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z, at least 50 steps.
- Save and load the document as plain .svg on disk via the File System Access API, with a localStorage autosave fallback.
- Export PNG at 1x, 2x, 4x by serializing the SVG into an offscreen image.

Explicitly out of scope, state this in the README:
- CMYK, spot colors, ICC profiles, Pantone, color separations.
- PDF, EPS, PostScript or PDF/X output.
- CDR or AI import.
- Multi-page layout, bitmap tracing, mesh fills, blends, envelopes.
- Font embedding. Text uses locally installed fonts only and will not travel.

Deliverables: npm install, npm run dev, a README that says plainly this is a toy next to Inkscape and lists the out-of-scope items above. No secrets needed, so no .env. Keyboard shortcuts documented in a help overlay bound to "?".
